arxiv-2201-02978.title: Auto-Encoder based Co-Training Multi-View Representation Learning Thanks: This work was supported by the National Key R&D Program of China (No. 2016YFC0303703).
arxiv-2201-02978.creator: Run-kun Lu, Jian-wei Liu, Yuan-fang Wang, Hao-jie Xie, Xin Zuo
arxiv-2201-02978.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Run-kun Lu, Jian-wei Liu, Yuan-fang Wang, Hao-jie Xie, Xin Zuo. Multi-view learning is a learning problem that utilizes the various representations of an object to mine valuable knowledge and improve the performance of learning algorithm, and one of the significant directions of multi-view learning is sub-space learning.

arxiv-2201-10267.title: On the Translation of Automata to Linear Temporal Logic Thanks: This is the full version of a chapter with the same title that appears in the FoSSaCS 2022 conference proceedings [ 5 ] .
arxiv-2201-10267.creator: Udi Boker, Karoliina Lehtinen, Salomon Sickert
arxiv-2201-10267.description: Abstract While the complexity of translating future linear temporal logic (LTL) into automata on infinite words is well-understood, the size increase involved in turning automata back to LTL is not. In particular, there is no known elementary bound on the complexity of translating deterministic ω \omega -regular automata to LTL.

arxiv-2204-08036.title: Federated Learning Cost Disparity for IoT Devices
arxiv-2204-08036.creator: Sheeraz A. Alvi † , Yi Hong ‡ , Salman Durrani †
arxiv-2204-08036.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) promotes predictive model training at the Internet of things (IoT) devices by evading data collection cost in terms of energy, time, and privacy. We model the learning gain achieved by an IoT device against its participation cost as its utility.

arxiv-2407-01320.title: Increasing Model Capacity for Free: A Simple Strategy for Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning
arxiv-2407-01320.creator: Haobo Song, Hao Zhao, Soumajit Majumder, Tao Lin
arxiv-2407-01320.description: Abstract Fine-tuning large pre-trained foundation models, such as the 175B GPT-3, have attracted more attention for downstream tasks recently. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods have been proposed and proven effective without retraining all model parameters, their performance is limited by the capacity of incremental modules, especially under constrained parameter budgets.

arxiv-2407-21641.title: Enhancing the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm in systems with large condition numbers
arxiv-2407-21641.creator: Peniel Bertrand Tsemo, Akshaya Jayashankar, K. Sugisaki, Nishanth Baskaran, Sayan Chakraborty, V. S. Prasannaa
arxiv-2407-21641.description: Abstract Although the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm offers an exponential speedup in system size for treating linear equations of the form A ​ x → = b → A\vec{x}=\vec{b} on quantum computers when compared to their traditional counterparts, it faces a challenge related to the condition number ( κ \mathcal{\kappa} ) scaling of the A A matrix.

arxiv-2410-21137.title: Search for excited tau leptons in the \PGt ​ \PGt ​ \PGg \PGt\PGt\PGg final state in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2410-21137.description: Abstract Results are presented for a test of the compositeness of the heaviest charged lepton, \PGt , using data collected by the CMS experiment in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV at the CERN LHC. The data were collected in 2016–2018 and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv .

arxiv-2502-18348.title: Towards softer ware: Enabling personalization of interactive data representations for users with disabilities Journal: IT Professional
arxiv-2502-18348.creator: Frank Elavsky, Marita Vindedal, Ted Gies, Patrick Carrington, Dominik Moritz, Øystein Moseng
arxiv-2502-18348.description: Abstract Accessible design for some may still produce barriers for others. This tension, called access friction, creates challenges for both designers and end-users with disabilities. To address this, we present the concept of softerware, a system design approach that provides end users with agency to meaningfully customize and adapt interfaces to their needs.

arxiv-2509-12280.title: The Emergence of Objective Classicality: A Computational First-Principles Study of Observer-Induced Decoherence in Unitary Quantum Mechanics
arxiv-2509-12280.creator: Eyad I.B Hamid
arxiv-2509-12280.description: Abstract The quantum measurement problem, the unresolved conflict between the unitary evolution of the wave function and the postulate of wave function collapse, remains the most profound conceptual challenge in quantum foundations. While environment-induced decoherence provides a compelling practical mechanism for the appearance of collapse, it does not resolve the fundamental issue of the observer’s own quantum state.

arxiv-2512-04988.title: Strategic Self-Improvement for Competitive Agents in AI Labour Markets
arxiv-2512-04988.creator: Christopher Chiu, Simpson Zhang & Mihaela van der Schaar
arxiv-2512-04988.description: Abstract As artificial intelligence (AI) agents are deployed across economic domains, understanding their strategic behavior and market-level impact becomes critical. This paper puts forward a groundbreaking new framework that is the first to capture the real-world economic forces that shape agentic labor markets: adverse selection, moral hazard, and reputation dynamics.

arxiv-2602-14080.title: Empty Shelves or Lost Keys? Recall Is the Bottleneck for Parametric Factuality
arxiv-2602-14080.creator: Nitay Calderon, Eyal Ben-David, Zorik Gekhman, Eran Ofek, Gal Yona
arxiv-2602-14080.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Nitay Calderon, Eyal Ben-David, Zorik Gekhman, Eran Ofek, Gal Yona. Standard factuality evaluations of LLMs treat all errors alike, obscuring whether failures arise from missing knowledge (empty shelves) or from limited access to encoded facts (lost keys).

pmc-10531635.title: Recent Mechanistic Studies in Allergic Diseases
pmc-10531635.creator: Sayantani B. Sindher, Reyna Sharma, Medha Yarlagadda, Andrew R. Chin, R. Sharon Chinthrajah
pmc-10531635.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The recent Special Issue in IJMS, entitled “Immunometabolism and Immunologic Mechanisms in Allergy Diseases”, features two excellent reviews that delve into the mechanisms implicated in cow’s milk allergies and mast cell responses in allergic diseases. Additionally, the Special Issue includes four research papers that explore recent advances in understanding the molecular mechanisms promoting allergic diseases, elucidating novel therapeutic strategies that could be employed for the better management and treatment of allergic disease.

pmc-11352204.title: Peritoneal Infusion of Oxygen Microbubbles Alters the Metabolomic Profile of the Lung and Spleen in Acute Hypoxic Exposure
pmc-11352204.creator: Christina Lisk, Alex Fan, Francesca I. Cendali, Kenta Kakiuchi, Delaney Swindle, David I. Pak, Robert Tolson, Abby Grier, Keely Buesing, Seth Zaeske, Angelo D’Alessandro, Mark A. Borden, David C. Irwin
pmc-11352204.description: Administration of oxygen microbubbles (OMBs) has been shown to increase oxygen and decrease carbon dioxide in systemic circulation, as well as reduce lung inflammation and promote survival in preclinical models of hypoxia caused by lung injury. However, their impact on microenvironmental oxygenation remains unexplored.

pmc-11361303.title: Microbial Ecology and Metabolism of Emerging Adulthood: Gut Microbiome Insights from a College Freshman Cohort
pmc-11361303.creator: Alex E. Mohr, Paniz Jasbi, Irene van Woerden, Jinhua Chi, Haiwei Gu, Meg Bruening, Corrie M. Whisner
pmc-11361303.description: The human gut microbiome (GM) undergoes dynamic changes throughout life, transitioning from infancy to adulthood. Despite improved understanding over the past years about how genetics, lifestyle, and the external environment impact the GM, limited research has explored the GM’s evolution during late-stage adolescence, especially among college students.

pmc-12650400.title: Assessing Vascular Tone and Fluid Balance in Septic and Cardiogenic Shock: A Feasibility Study on Skin Water Loss as a Diagnostic Tool
pmc-12650400.creator: Sabrina Kopp, Ingo Sagoschen, Susanne Helena Karbach, Martin Russwurm, Philipp Lurz, Thomas Münzel, Johannes Wild
pmc-12650400.description: Background/Objectives: Fluid management in shock remains a clinical challenge, with ongoing debate about optimal guidance. Despite advanced technologies, fluid balance assessment is often inadequate. The SkInShock study investigated whether transepidermal water loss (TEWL) measurements could improve fluid balance estimation and serve as a non-invasive marker of vascular tone in patients with septic or cardiogenic shock.

pmc-12715251.title: Metformin mitigates aortic valve degeneration in an ex vivo three-dimensional tissue model
pmc-12715251.creator: Friederike Irmgard Schoettler, Andreas Weber, Vera Schmidt, Sebastian Johannes Bauer, Moritz Benjamin Immohr, Artur Lichtenberg, Payam Akhyari, Mareike Barth
pmc-12715251.description: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent valvular disorder that lacks effective pharmacological treatments. Metformin, an oral anti-diabetic drug, has been suggested to protect valvular interstitial cells (VICs) from calcification, but its role in preventing organic phosphate-induced degeneration in VICs and aortic valve (AV) leaflets remains unclear.

pmc-12836907.title: Utility of 18F-Florzolotau PET as a prognostic and monitoring biomarker in a memory clinic cohort
pmc-12836907.creator: Jiaying Lu, Jie Wang, Huiwei Zhang, Jie Wu, Yunhao Yang, Min Wang, Xiaoxi Ma, Weiqi Bao, Zhenxu Xiao, Huamei Lin, Xiaowen Zhou, Zizhao Ju, Shumeng Yan, Fangyang Jiao, Xiaoniu Liang, Yang Liu, Li Zheng, Ming Li, Jingjie Ge, Ding Ding, Tzu-Chen Yen, Yihui Guan, Chuantao Zuo, Qianhua Zhao
pmc-12836907.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundTau PET is increasingly recognized for its prognostic and disease-monitoring value in Alzheimer’s disease (AD); however, real-world evidence in heterogeneous memory clinic populations remains limited, especially for novel tau positron emission tomography (PET) with 18F-Florzolotau.MethodsWe prospectively enrolled 340 individuals (patients with cognitive complaints and community volunteers) undergoing baseline amyloid PET and tau PET with 18F-Florzolotau, with subsets for clinical follow-up (n = 260; median interval 1.45 [0.96–2.56] years) and repeat tau PET (n = 64; median interval 2.27 [1.47–2.88] years).

pmc-13621298.title: High-resolution computed tomography assessment of connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: Advances in diagnosis and prognostic evaluation
pmc-13621298.creator: Si-Yu Jiang, Kai-Xiang Su, Cai-Feng Pang, Yu-Qing Tang, Yu-Jie Xiang, Ju Han, Yong-Long He, Rui Li
pmc-13621298.description: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), an important pulmonary manifestation of systemic autoimmune diseases and a major determinant of morbidity and mortality, is highly heterogeneous across disease subtypes, requiring reliable imaging assessment. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) remains the cornerstone imaging modality in this setting.
